package_info.package_manager: N/A (malicious Windows executable dropper distributed via web downloads)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (malware campaign, not a versioned package)
package_info.why_malicious: NullMixer is a malicious dropper that masquerades as legitimate software installers and is distributed via malicious websites using SEO poisoning. When executed, it silently drops and runs multiple embedded malware families (such as RedLine Stealer, SmokeLoader, Vidar, and others), leading to system compromise, credential theft, data exfiltration, and installation of additional malware. Its distribution method, payload delivery, and anti-forensic techniques make it a high-impact threat.

execution_context.file_location: Extracted executable from password-protected ZIP archive

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The dropper executable, when run, silently extracts and executes multiple embedded malware binaries (e.g., RedLine Stealer, SmokeLoader, Vidar, etc.) to the system, often to temporary or system directories.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the user-executed installer silently writes multiple embedded malware payloads to disk and launches them as separate processes, resulting in the installation and execution of various malware families and initiating further malicious activity.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The installer silently deploys and executes multiple unrelated malware binaries without user knowledge or consent, which is a hallmark of malicious droppers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers only install the intended software and do not deploy or execute unrelated executables, especially without user notification.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software bundles may install multiple components, but always with user consent, clear disclosure, and typically only related software.
key_indicators: Silent extraction and execution of multiple unrelated binaries
No user notification or consent for additional payloads
Payloads match known malware hashes or signatures
Writes executables to system or temporary directories

execution_context.file_location: Dropped malware binaries (e.g., RedLine Stealer, SmokeLoader, etc.)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Dropped payloads (e.g., RedLine Stealer) enumerate system information, harvest credentials, and exfiltrate data to hardcoded C2 domains/IPs.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After being dropped and executed, the malware payloads enumerate system information, access credential stores and sensitive files, and transmit harvested data to attacker-controlled C2 servers via outbound network connections.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting credentials and exfiltrating sensitive data to external servers is a core behavior of information-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not access credential stores or transmit user data to untrusted, hardcoded remote servers without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise management tools may collect system information, but only with user awareness and transmission to trusted, internal endpoints.
key_indicators: Network connections to known C2 infrastructure immediately after execution
Access to credential stores and sensitive files (e.g., browser data, system info)
Data exfiltration routines targeting hardcoded domains/IPs
Enumeration of environment variables and system configuration

execution_context.trigger: runtime (initial execution of dropper, post-payload deployment)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The dropper deletes itself and/or temporary files after execution to hinder forensic analysis.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After deploying and executing malware payloads, the dropper initiates self-deletion and removes temporary artifacts from disk, thereby evading detection and hindering post-infection forensic analysis.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Self-deletion and removal of execution traces are anti-forensic techniques commonly used by malware to avoid detection and impede investigation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers do not erase themselves or their logs after installation, as this would prevent troubleshooting and auditing.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate updaters may clean up temporary files, but do not delete the installer itself or remove evidence of installation.
key_indicators: Self-deletion routines invoked after payload execution
Immediate removal of dropped files and logs
Absence of installer or related artifacts post-execution

attack_chain.action: User visits a malicious website and downloads a password-protected ZIP archive masquerading as legitimate software.
attack_chain.leads_to: User extracts and executes the dropper executable.

attack_chain.action: User executes the dropper, which silently extracts and executes multiple embedded malware payloads.
Dropped malware payloads (stealers, backdoors, etc.) enumerate system information, harvest credentials, and exfiltrate data to C2 servers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive data and compromised systems.

attack_chain.action: Dropper deletes itself and temporary files to evade detection and hinder forensic analysis.
attack_chain.leads_to: Reduces evidence of infection, making detection and response more difficult.

behavioral_signatures: Installer or executable that silently drops and executes multiple unrelated binaries during installation
Silent installation of known malware families without user notification
Immediate self-deletion of the installer or removal of temporary files after execution
Execution of binaries from extracted password-protected archives
file_indicators: Password-protected ZIP archives containing suspicious executables masquerading as legitimate installers
Executables with hashes matching known NullMixer, RedLine Stealer, SmokeLoader, Vidar, and other malware families
Unexpected binaries written to system or temporary directories during installation process
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known C2 domains/IPs (e.g., azilominehostz.xyz, dll1.stdcdn.com, 185.186.142.166) immediately after installer execution
Network traffic to suspicious or newly registered domains following installation
Data exfiltration attempts to hardcoded remote endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for execution of installer files extracted from password-protected archives, especially those downloaded from unofficial or suspicious sources. Flag any installer that writes and executes multiple unrelated binaries or matches known malware hashes. Correlate file creation and process execution events with known IOCs. Monitor for outbound network connections to known C2 infrastructure or suspicious domains immediately after installer execution. Alert on self-deleting executables or installers that remove their own traces post-installation, and investigate any evidence of credential or data exfiltration.
